summary: No official Eritrean page we could read says which nationalities need a visa; the UK, Canadian, Australian, Irish and Serbian governments say their citizens need one to enter. The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says a visa is issued ten working days after it receives the application and fee, and that issue is not assured. The UK FCDO says foreign nationals need a permit to travel outside the Asmara region.

passportValidity.text: Your passport should be valid for at least 6 months on arrival in Eritrea. The Eritrean embassy asks for at least three blank pages for the visa.

source.name: UK FCDO — Eritrea travel advice, entry requirements

alsoStatedOn.name: Embassy and Permanent Mission of the State of Eritrea in Geneva — Visa & Travel Services

source.name: Embassy of the State of Eritrea in Switzerland — Visa and travel services

conflict.name: UK FCDO — Eritrea travel advice, entry requirements
conflict.states: at least 2 blank consecutive pages for stamping

vaccinations.name: Yellow fever
vaccinations.certificate: International Certificate of Vaccination or Prophylaxis (yellow card)
vaccinations.text: A yellow fever certificate is required from travelers arriving from countries with a risk of yellow fever transmission.

source.name: WHO, International Travel and Health, Annex 1 — countries requiring proof of vaccination against yellow fever
source.instrument: International Health Regulations (2005), Article 36 and Annex 7; WHO International Travel and Health, Annex 1, 18 November 2022 (revised 3 January 2023)

travelInsurance.text: No official source we could read states a travel insurance requirement for entering Eritrea. The UK government says public hospitals outside Asmara are often poorly equipped and rural facilities even more limited, and advises insurance that covers local treatment and medical evacuation.

source.name: UK Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office — Eritrea travel advice: health

onwardTicket.text: No official source we could read states a return or onward ticket requirement. The Embassy in Switzerland asks tourist visa applicants for a hotel or apartment reservation and proof of financial support, not a ticket.

source.name: Embassy of the State of Eritrea in Switzerland — Visa and travel services

proofOfFunds.text: Tourist visa applicants must include proof of financial support with the application. No amount is published.

source.name: Embassy of the State of Eritrea in Switzerland — Visa and travel services

currencyLimits.text: Foreign cash or travellers' cheques worth USD 10,000 or more must be declared on arrival; keep the certificate you are given to show when you leave. On departure you must be able to show that any foreign currency you spent was exchanged at Himbol, the state exchange, or spent at an official hotel, and you may not take more than 1,000 nakfa out of Eritrea.

The UK FCDO says you must declare all laptops, mobile phones, cameras and other electronic items on arrival, or they can be confiscated when you leave.

payments.text: The Government of Canada says Eritrea has a cash-based economy and that credit cards are not accepted for everyday transactions. Paying in foreign currency is illegal except at official hotels, which expect euros or US dollars; exchange money only at Himbol (the state exchange), main banks or major hotels in Asmara.

safety.text: Asmara is a relatively safe city, though there is a risk of street crime, especially at night. The UK advises against all travel within 25 km of Eritrea's land borders; foreign nationals need a permit to travel outside the Asmara region, and consular assistance is severely limited.

tips.text: The UK FCDO says foreign nationals must apply in advance for a permit to travel outside Asmara’s surrounding province, Zoba Maekel, and to some sites in the capital such as the tank graveyard. Tourists apply to the Ministry of Tourism; processing can take several days, permits are not always granted, and they are checked at checkpoints outside Asmara.

The UK FCDO advises against all travel within 25 km of Eritrea’s borders with Djibouti, Ethiopia and Sudan; the Australian government says landmines are found within 25 km of the border with Ethiopia.

The Government of Canada says credit cards are not accepted for everyday transactions and that money should be exchanged only through Himbol, main banks or major hotels; the UK FCDO says foreign currency must be declared on arrival and that you must be able to account for foreign currency spent when you leave.

The UK FCDO says internet access is highly restricted and mostly limited to hotels and a few internet cafes, there is no 3G, international SIM cards do not work, and a local SIM requires a residence permit.

Photographing government buildings and military installations is illegal (UK FCDO), and the Government of Canada also lists airports, ports and uniformed service members. The UK FCDO says to always ask before taking photos in any area where security personnel are present.

faq.question: Do I need a visa for Eritrea?
faq.answer: No official Eritrean page we could read says which nationalities need a visa. The UK, Canadian, Australian, Irish and Serbian governments say their citizens need one to enter. The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says a visa is issued ten working days after it receives the application and fee, and that issue is not assured.

faq.question: How long does an Eritrean visa take?
faq.answer: The Eritrean Embassy in Switzerland says a visa is issued ten working days after it receives the application and fee, and is valid for three months from issue. Approval is not guaranteed.

faq.question: Can I travel outside Asmara in Eritrea?
faq.answer: Only with a travel permit. The UK FCDO says foreign nationals need a permit, applied for in advance, to travel outside Asmara’s surrounding province (Zoba Maekel) and to some sites in the capital. Tourists apply to the Ministry of Tourism; processing can take several days, permits are not always granted, and they are checked at checkpoints.

faq.question: Can I use cards or ATMs in Eritrea?
faq.answer: No for everyday purchases: the Government of Canada says credit cards are not accepted for everyday transactions and Eritrea runs on cash. Declare foreign currency on arrival, exchange it only at Himbol, main banks or major hotels, and keep the receipts — the UK FCDO says you must account for foreign currency spent when you leave.

faq.question: Is Eritrea safe to visit?
faq.answer: The UK FCDO says Asmara is a relatively safe city, though there is a risk of street crime especially at night. It advises against all travel within 25 km of the land borders, says movement outside the Asmara region needs a permit and international SIM cards do not work, and that consular help is severely limited.
